intro: Click a state to see hourly load forecasts for its grid zone (not the state): past days from {pastStart} to {pastEnd} and a snapshot of future days.
snapshot: **Future forecast snapshot:** Forecast generated on {gen}, covers {first} to {last} ({d1} to {d2} Berlin dates). It is a one-off file made from real weather forecasts and the latest load known at {origin}; this page does not update itself and your browser makes no weather requests. Days 1–16 are forecasts; days 17–21 are a low-confidence outlook without weather. Accuracy falls the further ahead you look.
licences_load: Load and official forecast: {smard}, {ccby}; quarter-hourly values summed to hourly (changed), used to train and evaluate the models.
licences_weather: Weather input: {openmeteo}, {ccby}, averaged over three cities per zone.
licences_models: The forecasts shown are from the locked {lightgbm} models of this project (see the repository README and results/EXPERIMENTS.md).
licences_zones: Zone sources: SMARD "Control area" ({controlarea}); Deutscher Bundestag, Wissenschaftliche Dienste, WD 5 - 3000 - 117/16 (2017).
map_section_aria: Map of the 16 German states coloured by grid zone
how_1: Hover a state to see which grid zone it belongs to. All states of the same zone light up together.
how_2: Click the state to open its forecast window.
how_3: Pick a date. Past days show the real data; future days show a forecast only.
how_4: Pick an hour, or keep “Full day” to see all hours.
how_5: Read the chart: the black line is the real data, the orange line is our forecast, and the shaded bands are the usual range (darker band: likely range, 80%; lighter band: wide range, 95%). Future days have no black line because they have not happened yet.
how_zones: Zone colours show the dominant grid zone of each state. Some states are shared between two zones (shown in the popup). Grid zones follow the transmission operators' control areas, not state borders.
disclaimer_1: Every forecast is for the grid zone, not the state.
disclaimer_2: The ranges are narrower than their labels suggest.
disclaimer_3: Future days are a one-off snapshot, and accuracy falls the further ahead you look.
zone_stmt: Forecast is for the {zone} grid zone, not the state.
split_stmt: {state} is split between grid zones. The dominant zone used here is {zone} (a judgement from qualitative sources, not a measured share); part of {state} is also served by {others}. The numbers below are for the whole {zone} grid zone (which spans several states), not for {state} alone.
chart_aria: Actual and forecast load for the selected day with 80% and 95% ranges
backtest_note: Backtest using observed weather, not a live forecast.
badge_val: Validation period (used for tuning and calibration)
badge_mixed: Mixed day: {nVal} h in the validation period (used for tuning and calibration), {nTest} h in the unseen test period
badge_outlook: Low-confidence outlook – has not happened yet
nodata_gap: No data for this date: the past data end on {lastPast} (the newest weeks were held back as unsettled) and the forecast snapshot starts on {firstFuture}.
nodata_after: No forecast for this date: the snapshot ends on {lastFuture}.
nodata_other: This date is outside the covered range or all its hours are missing.
missing_hours: {n} hour(s) of this date are left out: the actual load for the hour, or for the same hour one or two weeks earlier (a model input), is missing in the source data.
cov_stmt: Measured on the unseen test year: the 80% range contained {m80} of actual values and the 95% range {m95} (mean of the four zones; {zone}: {z80} and {z95}). The ranges are narrower than their labels suggest.
row_horizon_val: {d} (counted from the last known load hour; model for day {k})
future_info: **Forecast generated on {gen}**, covers {first} to {last}. Days ahead for this date: **{hz}** (counted from the last known load hour, {origin}). This is a static snapshot, not live; there is no actual line because these hours had not happened when it was made.
future_partial: This date is only partly covered by the snapshot.
acc_intro: **How accurate is this horizon?** Accuracy falls the further ahead you look. For {zone} the average error in the unseen test year was {a1} for the 1-day model and {aL} for the {L}-day model (the simple same-hour-last-week baseline: {b1} and {bL}). The 17–21 day outlook is low-confidence.
cfg_A: no weather inputs (calendar and recent load only)
cfg_B: a forecast of temperature plus calendar and recent load
cfg_C: forecasts of temperature, humidity, wind, solar radiation and cloud plus calendar and recent load
acc_warn: **The ranges are too narrow.** On the unseen test year the 80% ranges contained about 72% and the 95% ranges about 90% of actual values at every horizon, and some zones were worse (TenneT 66% and 86%). Treat the ranges as optimistic.
acc_weather: Weather: archived weather forecasts were only available for leads up to 7 days, so only days 1–7 can use a weather forecast, and only where it helped on validation (see the Inputs column; in most cases it did not). Days 8–21 use calendar and recent load only. Validation = {v0} to {v1} (exclusive); the test year was used for the load-only 24-hour model before and is now a second time for these models. Weather forecasts for days 1–7 come from Open-Meteo; the models were trained on older archived forecasts of the same kind (which may differ from today's forecast model mix).
load_error: Sorry, the map data could not be loaded. Please check your connection and reload the page. (Technical detail: {err}) If you are running this folder on your own computer, serve it over http, e.g. {cmd}, and open {url}; browsers block opening index.html directly via file://.
snapshot_ended: This forecast snapshot ended on {date}, so it is no longer current.
today_nearest: Today is not available here, so the nearest available date is shown: {date}.
tip_latest: Jump to the most recent day that has real (measured) data.
tip_today: Jump to today's date in Berlin time, if it is covered.
head_past_day: On {date} the real average was {actual} and our forecast was {fc} ({pct} off).
head_past_hour: On {date} at {hour} the real value was {actual} and our forecast was {fc} ({pct} off).
range_hint: The ranges tend to be a bit too narrow – see details.
load_error_zone: Sorry, the data for this grid zone could not be loaded. Please check your connection and try again. ({err})
privacy_line: This site collects no personal data and sets no cookies; your language choice is kept only in your own browser. The web host may keep standard technical server logs.
meta_description: Interactive map of Germany: hourly electricity-load forecasts for the four grid zones, for past days and as a snapshot of future days. Not production-grade.
